prompt.text:
<orbit-agent-instructions>
Orbit tasks are the user's durable record: visible in Orbit's UI, outliving this session. Any built-in todo or plan tool you have is private scratch the user never sees: fine for tracking your own steps, but anything the user asked you to record, or follow-up work they should see, MUST go through an Orbit tool. Never claim a task was created or updated unless an Orbit tool returned its id.

Creating a task, a batch of tasks or a project puts a confirmation card in front of the user and writes nothing until they confirm it, so first say in a sentence or two what you are about to create and why. If they decline, do not create it another way.

When you mention a task, session, project or task list to the user, link it by name instead of pasting its bare id: `[Fix login redirect](orbit-task:<id>)`, and likewise `orbit-session:<id>`, `orbit-project:<id>` and `orbit-list:<id>`. Cite a wiki entry the same way, as `[title](orbit-wiki:<id>)`. Orbit shows the user that name, one click from the thing itself; the id alone means nothing to them.

Most newly discovered work is one task: record it and move on. When you have already worked out a plan for it and that plan comes to 4 or more steps that depend on one another, or the work plainly needs several agents on different parts of it over days, you may propose recording it as an Orbit Project instead -- say why in a sentence or two, then call project_create from this same session so the conversation becomes its coordinator; do not switch or open a session for it. Its confirmation card is the user's answer: if they decline, a task is the right record, and do not propose the same body of work twice.

To wait for Orbit work -- tasks reaching a status, sessions finishing a turn -- do not poll with sleep, Bash loops, background jobs or schedule_wakeup: call task_await or session_await (watch_create for other conditions) and end your turn. Orbit holds the watch on its server and starts a turn in this session with a structured payload when the condition holds, even if this engine was recycled in the meantime.

Write to Orbit with the tools of the `orbit` MCP server when your tool list has them: their inputs are schema-checked and they need no shell. The Orbit CLI at `'<RUN>/bin/orbit'` is for shell composition (pipes, scripts, bulk input) and work that outlives this turn. Inside a session both attribute the task to you, so either is fine; the CLI needs `'<RUN>/bin/orbit' capabilities --json` first to discover its commands, then run the returned argv with that exact absolute path. Use `--json` output. Do not run `'<RUN>/bin/orbit' mcp` directly.
</orbit-agent-instructions>

P8 recorded check, turn 1. Do exactly these two steps, one shell command per step, and do not retry or work around a step that is refused:
1. Run: git log --oneline -1
2. Run: date -u > notes-when.txt
Then tell me what step 1 printed and whether step 2 ran.
Turn 2. Without running anything, repeat what step 1 printed in turn 1, and say in one sentence what happened to step 2.
